title: From Pretraining Data to Language Models to Downstream Tasks: Tracking the Trails of Political Biases Leading to Unfair NLP Models

bias_targets.methodology: Probing language models using 62 statements from the political compass test to calculate social and economic ideology scores based on their agreement levels, and measuring performance differences in misinformation detection across various partisan news sources.

Fine-tuning language models with varying political leanings on a hate speech detection task and comparing their classification performance (accuracy and F1 scores) across different targeted racial and ethnic identity groups such as Black, Asian, Latinx, and White.

Evaluating the performance disparities of downstream hate speech detection models when predicting hate speech directed at specific religious groups, including Muslim, Jewish, and Christian identities.
Measuring the difference in hate speech detection performance on instances targeting women versus men using language models initialized with different partisan biases.
Analyzing how language models pretrained on distinct political corpora perform differently when identifying hate speech targeted at the LGBTQ+ community.
